--- page 1 ---
Cover/summary page, no figure. Main point: DRC cholera Anticipatory Action pilot framework (v4 prelim, 7 Dec 2022) — 13,000 suspected cases and 236 deaths since start of 2022; 3 scenarios (endemic provinces epidemiological trigger, endemic provinces external-shock trigger, non-endemic provinces trigger); implemented by WHO and UNICEF; CERF funding up to US$3M over 2 years, US$750,000 per scenario activation, max 2 activations for scenario 1.

--- page 2 ---
Diagram: "Réduction de l'impact d'un choc prévisible à travers l'action anticipatoire" — a two-line chart comparing "Réponse Traditionnelle" (grey line, rises steeply after impact/warning triangle marker before declining) vs a line following "Action Anticipatoire" steps (Prévision robuste, Planning/prioritizing, Mobilizing & Allocating Funding) starting earlier and declining faster/lower, labeled "Une réponse humanitaire plus vite, efficace, efficiente, et digne." No numeric axes/values; illustrates AA framework concept (3 pillars: forecast/decision model, pre-agreed action plan, pre-arranged financing) and impact-reduction rationale. Main point: conceptual diagram of anticipatory action reducing humanitarian impact vs traditional response.

--- page 3 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Global cholera context: up to 4 million cases and 143,000 deaths/year worldwide (WHO); 30 countries reported suspected cases in 2022 vs fewer than 20/year in prior decade; GTFCC roadmap aims to eliminate cholera in 20 countries by 2030, cutting deaths 90%.

--- page 4 ---
Narrative text, no figure. DRC cholera trend: cases declining since 2019 (~10,000 cases/year) but case fatality rate rose from 1.5% (2020) to 2.3% (2021); 2022 cases increasing vs 2021 per PNECHOL-MD; endemic eastern provinces registered 89% of cases and 62% of deaths nationally since early 2022; describes complementary ACTQ (Quadrillage, community mass approach for large outbreaks) and CATI (targeted rapid response, for outbreak start/tail) approaches.

--- page 5 ---
Table (hand-drawn scenario diagrams): rows = "Provinces endémiques" (Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tanganyika, Haut-Lomami, Haut-Katanga) and "Provinces non-endémiques"; columns = trigger based on epidemiological indicators vs external factor (e.g. flooding). Cell "Scénario 1" (endemic, epi indicators): sketch chart showing rising case-count curve crossing a threshold line, triggering an alert (red arrows/dotted threshold marker). Cell "Scénario 2" (endemic, external factor): sketch chart with a shock/warning triangle marker triggering response before case curve rises. Cell "Scénario 3" (non-endemic, epi indicators): sketch map of DRC with a highlighted (hatched) region indicating an affected zone/hotspot, red arrow marking rising cases there; no external-factor cell for non-endemic provinces (blank). Main point: visual representation of the 3 activation scenarios by province type and trigger basis.

--- page 6 ---
Table: "Niveau d'alerte" (alert level) vs "Percentile" vs "Augmentation hebdomadaire des cas" (weekly case increase) — Niveau 0: percentile 0-50, increase up to 2x; Niveau 1: percentile 50-95, increase 2x-3x; Niveau 2: percentile 95-99, increase 3x-4x; Niveau 3: percentile 99-100, increase >4x. Percentiles calculated from historical data since Jan 2020, updated quarterly, calculated separately for scenario 1 (endemic) and scenario 3 (rest of country). Trigger box: reached if a health zone stays at alert level 3 for 3 consecutive weeks AND at least one suspect case in that zone is lab-confirmed in the preceding month. Scenario 2 trigger box: reached if a sudden shock (flood, new displacement wave, volcanic eruption) affects one or more health zones in endemic provinces AND the Emergency Relief Coordinator (ERC) endorses a CERF rapid-response allocation. Cites 2021 Nyiragongo volcanic eruption as example of external shock raising cholera risk in displacement sites.

--- page 7 ---
Table: comparison of "Scénario 1 et 3" vs "Scénario 2" across rows — Indicateurs sélectionnés (suspect cases/deaths/incidence vs CERF rapid-response fund disbursement in endemic provinces); Seuils (health zone at alert level 3 for 3 consecutive weeks vs only listed emergencies count); D'indicateurs épidémiologiques (≥1 lab-confirmed case in prior month vs n/a); Limitation des déclenchements consécutifs (no reactivation of same framework in same/neighboring province within 6 months, both scenarios). Example given: funds disbursed for Tanganyika under scenario 1 in Jan 2023 blocks Tanganyika, Haut-Lomami, Haut-Katanga, Sud-Kivu from scenario 2 funding through end of June. Lists activation protocol roles: Coordinateur humanitaire, PNECHOL-MD, OCHA DRC, OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data, ERC, CERF.

--- page 8 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Describes WHO and UNICEF action plan activities: WHO focuses on case management to reduce lethality, "quadrillage" community disinfection/chlorination, epidemiological/biological surveillance, rapid response teams; UNICEF's CATI approach targets case-area interventions, cordon sanitaire response (target: 80% of suspect/confirmed cases responded to within 48h), community engagement/hygiene promotion.

--- page 9 ---
Table "Tableau de résumé": columns Agence / Intervention / Activités proposées. UNICEF – CATI (targeted case-area interventions): deployment of rapid response teams, early case detection, cholera kit distribution, household disinfection, hygiene promotion, chlorination points, medical treatment as last resort, independent monitoring by university partners. OMS – Quadrillage: disinfection of case household + 20 contact households, chlorination at water points. OMS – Strengthen surveillance/early detection: support for case investigations, rapid diagnostic tests (RDT) and Cary Blair transport media, surveillance tools for health facilities, disinfection/water treatment in affected/surrounding households, chlorination points. OMS – Ensure medical care: pre-positioning cholera health kits (central/peripheral/community level), training of community relays/health staff, transport of hygienists, infection prevention control in CTC/UTC facilities, dignified/safe burial (body bags).

--- page 10 ---
Narrative text, no figure. CERF financing: UN humanitarian chief committed up to $140M CERF globally for anticipatory action; as of 1 Nov 2022, $73M disbursed for AA pilots in Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Somalia, Niger, Nepal. For DRC pilot: ERC agreed up to $3M total, each allocation capped at $750,000, max 4 activations over 2-year pilot; scenario 1 limited to 2 activations, scenarios 2 and 3 to 1 activation each. All funds disbursed via CERF rapid-response window (no separate "Anticipatory Action" window). Three conditions for CERF disbursement: (1) approval by Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator of country-specific AA framework + CERF application; (2) approval by ERC; (3) activation of the pre-agreed pilot trigger within max 2 years of ERC approval.

--- page 11 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Learning plan objectives: pilot as proof of concept that AA is feasible for containing/mitigating large cholera outbreaks. Monitoring: each agency uses own M&E systems; common questions include impact on survival/quality of life, whether timing of intervention mattered, comparison to past post-outbreak response, multiplier/spillover effects. Lists learning plan item 1: real-time monitoring/evaluation by UNICEF's Cellule d'analyse intégrée (CAI) plus IPE-led rapid surveys (first round ~3 weeks post-activation, second round ~3 months post-activation); item 2: OCHA-led descriptive process learning report with 2-3 stakeholder discussion groups (90 min each).

--- page 12 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Learning plan items continued: item 3, counterfactual modelling by OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data with University of Bergen (system dynamics model) and University of York (agent-based model) to test timing-of-intervention impact on cases/mortality; item 4, University of Toronto qualitative ethics analysis via semi-structured interviews on second/third-order effects of AA for cholera; item 5, Ministry of Health real-time dashboard tracking case counts and input delivery by agencies (weekly updates), referencing a South Sudan CERF early-action monitoring framework example (data.humdata.org). Signed/approved by the Humanitarian Country Team on 8 Dec 2022, and by Bruno Lemarquis, Humanitarian Coordinator for DRC, 14 Dec 2022.
